name: Brao-Krung / Krung
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source.
catalog_citation: Keller, Charles E. 2001. Brao-Krung phonology. Mon-Khmer Studies 31: 1-13. (SEAlang MKS archive scan,http://sealang.net/archives/mks/pdf/31:)
catalog_locator: p. 2, section 2 'Words and syllables' (also p. 5, section 2.2.1 'Syllable patterns')
catalog_quote: The phonological word in Krung exhibits the familar Mon-Khmer sesquisyllabic (Matisoff, 1989) structure, in which a strongly stressed Main Syllable (s̄) is optionally preceded by a weakly stressed Presyllable (s++), that is: Phonological Word [tree:] (Presyllable: S̆) + Main Syllable: Ś ... [p. 5, 2.2.1] Main syllables in sesquisyllabic words as well as monosyllabic forms in general take the following shape or some subset thereof: C(L/N)V(C) ... followed by a rhyme with a strongly stressed vocalic peak of syllabicity (V) and optionally closed by a restricted group (see Figure 2) of final consonants (C).
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.rule_in_words: Words are monosyllables or sesquisyllables (presyllable + main syllable); stress falls on the main syllable, which is the final syllable of the phonological word; the presyllable is weakly stressed with a reduced short vowel. No tone or register.
new_statements.secondary_stress: None described; presyllable characterised only as 'weakly stressed'.
new_statements.exceptions: None. (Maximal word is sesquisyllabic Cv(N/R).C(L/N)V(C); no polysyllabic native words discussed.)
new_statements.domain_note: Phonological word; statement is structural (sesquisyllabic template), not instrumental. Sidwell & Jacq 2003 p.33 give the same 'stressed mainsyllable preceded by a minorsyllable' characterisation for West Bahnaric as a whole.
new_statements.identity_note: Keller 2001 describes the Krung (Brao-Krung) dialect of Ratanakiri, Cambodia; Glottolog lave1249 'Brao' subsumes Krung, Kavet/Kravet, Taveng Brao and Laveh/Lave (Laos) as mutually intelligible dialects (Keller 2001 p.1; Sidwell & Jacq 2003 p.30). ISO has separate codes krr (Krung) and krv (Kavet) but Glottolog treats them under lave1249.

tone_statements.citation: Phan Lương Hùng. 2024. Hệ thống phụ âm đầu trong tiếng Brâu [The initial consonant system of Brâu]. Ngôn ngữ (Hà Nội: Viện Ngôn ngữ học) 2024(7): 11-16.
tone_statements.quote: Tạ Văn Thông, Tạ Quang Tùng [4] đề cập đến tiếng Brâu như là đại diện duy nhất của nhóm Laven - Brao, nhánh Bahnaric, chi Mon-Khmer, ngữ hệ Nam Á với các đặc điểm loại hình đơn lập, cận âm tiết tính và không có thanh điệu. ... Trong các phụ âm hữu thanh, ở vị trí cấu âm môi và lợi xuất hiện đối lập về chất giọng, bao gồm chất giọng thường /b, d, ɟ, r/ và chất giọng thở (breathy voice) /b̤, d̤/. Trong đó, chất giọng thở được cấu âm với dây thanh chùng, tần số dao động thấp hơn, luồng hơi đi qua thanh môn lớn hơn.
tone_statements.translation: Tạ Văn Thông & Tạ Quang Tùng [4] treat Brâu as the sole representative of the Laven-Brao group, Bahnaric branch, Mon-Khmer, Austroasiatic, with the typological traits: isolating, sesquisyllabic and without tones. ... Among the voiced consonants, at the labial and alveolar places of articulation there is a contrast in voice quality, comprising modal voice /b, d, ɟ, r/ and breathy voice /b̤, d̤/. Breathy voice is articulated with slack vocal folds, a lower vibration frequency and a larger airflow through the glottis.
tone_statements.locator: p. 11, sec. 2.2 'Lịch sử nghiên cứu' (no-tone characterisation, reported from ref. [4]); p. 15, sec. 4 (voicing/phonation classes, breathy-voiced stops); p. 16, sec. 5 'Kết luận' (25 phonemes; 'đối lập vô thanh - hữu thanh - thở' at labial and alveolar stops).
tone_statements.summary: No tones (secondhand typological statement endorsed in the literature review); synchronic phonation contrast located in onsets: voiceless /p t c k/ (+ aspirates) vs modal voiced /b d ɟ (g)/ vs breathy-voiced /b̤ d̤/ (lower F0, breathy airflow) -- an incipient register cue analysed as consonantal, matching Huffman 1976's description of breathiness after the voiced series; no vowel register, no ton…

sources.note: (i) reports Tạ Văn Thông & Tạ Quang Tùng 2017 characterising Brâu as isolating, sesquisyllabic and without tones ('không có thanh điệu'); (ii) own analysis: 25 initial consonant phonemes with a three-way voiceless / voiced / breathy-voiced contrast at labial and alveolar places -- modal /b d ɟ r/ vs breathy 'chất giọng thở' /b̤ d̤/ (slack vocal folds, lower F0, greater airflow), e.g. bŭn 'lucky' vs b̤un 'to bank up earth'; the phonation contrast is assigned to the onsets, no vowel register or tone posited. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Huffman, Franklin E. 1976. The register problem in fifteen Mon-Khmer languages. In Philip N. Jenner, Laurence C. Thompson & Stanley Starosta (eds.), Austroasiatic Studies, Part I (Oceanic Linguistics Special Publication 13), 575-589. Honolulu: University Press of Hawaii.
sources.note: Brao retains the original voiced stop series /b d j g/ with slight aspiration/breathiness carrying into the following vowel ('somewhat voiceless and centralized') versus clear vowels after /p t c k/ and preglottalized stops; vowel differentiation is 'little or no', so Brao is classed A.1 'Conservative' (voicing contrast reflected in the initials), not a register language and not restructured/tonal. No statement on stress.

tone.quote: Brao is intermediate between Stage 1 and Stage 2 in preserving the voiced series /b d j g/, but which are accompanied by slight aspiration which carries through a following vowel, rendering it somewhat voiceless and centralized, in contrast with the clear vowel quality following /p t c k/ and preglottalized /ʔb ʔd ʔj/. ... A. Original voiced:voiceless distinction reflected in the initials: 1. Conservative (retention of original /b d j g/ little or no vowel differentiation): Loven, Lawa, Stieng, Brao
tone.locator: (p. 579 by page count; Brao paragraph following the Loven/Lawa/Stieng 'Stage 1' paragraphs) and (p. 587; final classification 'A.1 Conservative')
